explain.say: Start at a small family farm in Ghana. Cocoa trees grow in the shade in hot, wet places near the Equator. Farmers cut the big pods by hand and scoop out the beans. Ghana and its neighbour Côte d’Ivoire grow about 60 percent of the world’s cocoa. Can you find Ghana on a map?

explain.say: The beans ferment for about a week, then dry in the sun. Then they are packed into sacks and shipped across the ocean, many to the Netherlands, where Amsterdam is one of the biggest cocoa ports in the world. Why do you think the beans travel so far?

explain.say: In factories, the beans are roasted and ground into cocoa butter and powder. Then companies add sugar and milk and mould the bars. These steps add value, which means they make the product worth much more, and most happen in Europe and North America. Can you see where the money goes?

explain.say: The bar is sold in a shop near you, but the farmer gets only a small slice of the price, often around 6 percent. Great thinking! Good news: Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire are opening more of their own chocolate factories, so more value stays at home.

faq.a: Cocoa beans grow inside big pods on cocoa trees, which first grew wild in the Amazon rainforest. Today most cocoa is grown in West Africa, especially Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana, and also in Indonesia, Ecuador and Brazil.
asks: Which country grows the most cocoa?

faq.q: Why is cocoa processed in other countries?
faq.a: Most big chocolate companies, factories and machines are in Europe and North America, close to the shoppers. For a long time trade rules also made it cheaper to import raw beans than finished chocolate.
asks: Why doesn't Ghana make its own chocolate?

faq.q: How much of the chocolate price does the farmer get?
faq.a: Often only around 6 percent. Most of the price goes to the companies that make and sell the chocolate, to shops and to taxes.
asks: How much does a cocoa farmer get?

faq.a: Globalisation means countries becoming more connected through trade, travel, companies and the internet. A chocolate bar is a good example: grown in Africa, made in Europe, sold everywhere.
Fairtrade is a label that promises farmers a minimum price for their crop plus an extra payment for community projects, such as schools and clean water.

facts: Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana together grow about 60% of the world's cocoa.
The Port of Amsterdam is one of the largest cocoa ports in the world.
Cocoa trees first grew wild in the Amazon rainforest of South America.

quiz.why: These two West African neighbours grow most of the world’s cocoa.

wrong.1: Switzerland and Belgium make chocolate but grow no cocoa.

quiz.say: Why does the cocoa farmer get only a small share of the chocolate price?

options.show: Most money-making steps happen in factories and shops abroad
options.say: Most money-making steps happen in factories and shops abroad

options.show: Farmers give their beans away free
options.say: Farmers give their beans away free

quiz.why: Grinding, making, branding and selling chocolate add most of the value, and mostly happen far from the farm.

wrong.1: Farmers sell their beans, but at a low price.
wrong.2: Making chocolate costs a lot, which is where most of the price goes.
